description: This walk follows the coastal path from Chapel St Leonards to Ingoldmells. The route runs for just over 2 miles, heading south along the beaches and promenade connecting the two settlements. The journey offers a quintessential Lincolnshire coast experience, providing a flat and easy-access route that is perfect for families, dog walkers, and those looking for a breezy sea-front stroll. As you traverse the well-maintained promenade, you’ll enjoy panoramic views of the North Sea on one side and the charming coastal landscapes on the other. This path serves as a tranquil link between the quieter, village atmosphere of Chapel St Leonards and the lively, attraction-filled skyline of Ingoldmells.Despite the proximity to popular holiday parks, the area retains a significant natural appeal. The shoreline is a fantastic place to observe coastal wildlife; look out for grey seals often spotted bobbing in the surf close to the shore. The dunes and sea buckthorn scrub along the path provide shelter for a variety of songbirds, such as linnets and stonechats, while the beach itself is a busy feeding ground for curlews and ringed plovers.
